title: FilePaths unknown-drive sentinel
contracts: File_TranslateNtToDosPathForDatFile owns FilePaths.dat save-time path projection
File_TranslateDosToNtPathForDatFile owns FilePaths.dat load-time path projection
drive-letter mappings come from MS-DOS device namespace links
unavailable drive-letter paths must be preserved rather than silently dropped
the leading-backslash sentinel shape represents a preserved DOS drive-letter path with unknown NT target
save-time stripping is legal only when the colon immediately precedes the first path separator or terminator after the leading backslash
known NT paths still use MUP, drive, or UNC mapping
this SREV changes comments and proof only
local_edges: File_GetDriveForLetter succeeds -> store true NT path
File_GetDriveForLetter fails -> preserve DOS drive-letter sentinel
leading-backslash drive-letter sentinel -> strip one leading backslash before write
runtime_gate: Windows FilePaths.dat round trip with available drive, unavailable drive, UNC/MUP, volume serial suffix, and drive reappearance
